data.bottom_line: The avalanche danger is MODERATE for WIND SLABS above 3500'. The danger is LOW elsewhere. A modest amount of new snow accompanied by breezy winds has increased the potential for a skier or rider to trigger an avalanche in select areas at upper elevations. As you climb in elevation, be on the lookout for dense or stiff drifts. Slopes near ridgelines, the tops of alpine bowls, or along the sides of gullies are the most likely places to find trouble. You can seek slopes less than 30 degrees in steepness, or non-windloaded terrain to lessen your chances of triggering a slide. ------------------------------------ SPECIAL ANNOUNCEMENTS: State of the Snowpack: Thursday, December 3rd - 6PM @ Backcountry Bike and Ski Free Avalanche Rescue Workshop: Saturday, December 12th – 12PM-3PM @ Hatcher Pass – Fishhook (Marmot) Lot
